Isocyanates are compounds containing the functional group -N=C=O. When isocyanates burn or thermally decompose, they can produce several toxic gases due to their chemical composition:

1. Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN): Due to the carbon-nitrogen bonds in isocyanates
2. Nitrogen Oxides (NOx): Due to the nitrogen content in isocyanates
3. Carbon Monoxide (CO): From incomplete combustion of the carbon content
4. Sulfur Oxides (SOx): If the isocyanate contains sulfur compounds

Looking at the options:
A. CH4, C2H6 (methane, ethane) - These are simple hydrocarbons, not typically the main toxic products of isocyanate combustion
B. CO2, H2O (carbon dioxide, water) - These are normal combustion products of many organic compounds but not the toxic gases of concern
C. Cl2, Br2 (chlorine, bromine) - These would only be produced if the isocyanates contained chlorine or bromine, which is not inherent to isocyanates
D. HCN, NOx, SOx, CO - These are the toxic gases typically produced when isocyanates burn

The correct answer is D. HCN, NOx, SOx, CO.
